lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! I'd be happy to help you determine if you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some questions to assess eligibility:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of his exact age at the moment - he's a teenager, somewhere between 15 and 19, but I'd have to check his birth certificate for the exact date.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is a teenager between 15 and 19, his age is particularly important for Child Benefit eligibility as there are different rules at age 16.

Let me ask you this: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm afraid I don't really know what his current education situation is. He doesn't live with me, so I'm not sure if he's in school or college or what he might be doing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. It's helpful to know that Alex doesn't live with you.

Let me ask: **Who does Alex currently live with, and how long has he been living there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mother, my ex-partner. He's been living with her for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

**Is Alex's mother currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex lives with his mother, let me ask: **Do you make any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep?** (This could include things like maintenance payments, money for clothes, food, pocket money, or contributions towards his accommodation.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like his clothes, school supplies, and other things he needs - about £50 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's good to know you're contributing towards Alex's upkeep.

To properly assess your eligibility, I need to clarify a few more important details:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Leeds.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And one more important question:

**Are you currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?** (I'm asking because the rules are slightly different depending on whether you're already receiving it or if someone else was previously claiming and has stopped.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently receiving Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. 

Just to make sure I have a complete picture, let me ask: **Do you know if anyone else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (You mentioned his mother isn't claiming, but I want to confirm no one else is - for example, another relative or guardian.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, as far as I know, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Just his mother isn't claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. 

One final important question to help me assess your situation: **Roughly how long ago did Alex go to live with his mother?** (I'm trying to understand if this is a recent change or if he's been living with her for many months or years.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been living with her for quite a long time now - it's been years, not a recent thing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on all the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**The main rules for Child Benefit eligibility are:**
- You normally qualify if the child lives with you, OR
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent) towards their upkeep

While you do contribute £50 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is more than the Child Benefit amount of approximately £25.60 per week), the issue is that Alex has been living with his mother for years in a stable, long-established arrangement.

The rules do allow Child Benefit to continue when a child goes to live elsewhere if you're making sufficient contributions, but this provision is designed for situations where there's been a recent change in living arrangements and you maintain financial support during that transition period (initially for 8 weeks, or longer with contributions).

Since Alex has lived with his mother for years, this isn't a recent change situation. In these circumstances, **the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit is the person Alex lives with - his mother** - even though she has chosen not to claim it currently.

If circumstances change (for example, if Alex were to come and live with you), you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that point. You might also want to encourage Alex's mother to claim, as Child Benefit can provide valuable support and also protects National Insurance credits for the claimant's state pension.

reasonings:
According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child and you live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible for a child if either: (1) you live with them, or (2) you're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them.

In Alex's case: He does not live with you - he has been living with his mother for years. While you do contribute £50 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, school supplies, etc.), the current Child Benefit rate is approximately £25.60 for the eldest/only child and £16.95 for additional children per week. Your £50 weekly contribution exceeds the Child Benefit amount.

However, the critical issue is that the rules state you 'may be able to get Child Benefit' for up to 8 weeks after your child goes to live with someone else if nobody else claims. It can continue for longer if you make contributions to your child's upkeep equal to or greater than the Child Benefit payment. But this provision applies when there has been a change in living arrangements.

In your situation, Alex has been living with his mother for years - this is a long-established arrangement, not a recent change. The extended eligibility based on contributions is designed for situations where a child has recently gone to live elsewhere and the parent maintains financial support. Given that Alex has lived with his mother for years in a stable arrangement, and you do not live with him, you would not qualify for Child Benefit under the standard rules. The person who lives with Alex (his mother) would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit, even though she has chosen not to do so.

The appropriate claimant would be the person Alex lives with (his mother).
